title: EBS Performance Tuning & Snapshots ⚡
description: Maximise throughput and IOPS, automate backups, and understand snapshot cost.

slides.title: IOPS, Throughput, and Latency 📈
slides.content:
# Performance Metrics

- **IOPS (Input/Output Operations Per Second)**: measures how many reads/writes per second. Important for random small I/O (databases).
- **Throughput**: data volume transferred per second (MB/s). Important for sequential large I/O (big data).
- **Latency**: time for a single I/O operation. gp3 and io2 provide single‑digit millisecond latency.

EBS volume performance depends on:
- Volume type and size.
- Instance's EBS‑optimised bandwidth (larger instances have more dedicated EBS bandwidth).
- Workload pattern.

slides.title: gp3: The New Default 👑
slides.content:
# No More Performance Scaling with Size

Earlier gp2 volumes tied IOPS to volume size: 3 IOPS per GB, up to 16,000 IOPS. gp3 breaks that link:
- Baseline 3,000 IOPS and 125 MB/s throughput, regardless of size.
- You can provision up to 16,000 IOPS and 1,000 MB/s for an additional cost.
- Smaller volumes get much higher performance.

**Always choose gp3** for new general‑purpose volumes unless you have a specific reason.

quizData.question: A 50 GB gp2 volume provides what baseline IOPS?
quizData.explanation: gp2 formula: 3 IOPS per GB. 50 GB × 3 = 150 IOPS. gp3 gives 3,000 IOPS baseline regardless of size.

slides.title: EBS Snapshots: Incremental Backups 📸
slides.content:
# Point‑in‑Time Copies

Snapshots capture the state of a volume at a specific moment. They are:
- **Incremental**: only changed blocks are stored after the first full snapshot.
- **Stored in S3** (AWS‑managed, not visible).
- Can be used to create new volumes or copy volumes across AZs/regions.
- Can be automated with **Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (DLM)**.

When you delete a snapshot, only the data unique to that snapshot is removed.

slides.title: Creating a Snapshot Lifecycle Policy ⏰
slides.content:
# Automate with DLM

Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager lets you create policies that automatically:
- Take snapshots every X hours/days.
- Retain the last N snapshots (rolling backup).
- Apply tags to snapshots.

Example: daily snapshot at 2 AM, retain 7 days, all instances tagged `Backup=true`.

slides.title: EBS Encryption 🔐
slides.content:
# At Rest and In Transit

EBS volumes can be encrypted using KMS. Encryption is:
- Transparent: you don't change your application.
- Encrypts data at rest, in flight between instance and volume, and all snapshots.
- Minimal impact on latency.
- Can be enabled by default for all new volumes in a region.

You can't encrypt an existing unencrypted volume directly; you snapshot it, copy the snapshot with encryption, then create a new volume.

slides.title: Pro Tip: RAID on EBS for Extreme Performance 🚀
slides.content:
## Combine Volumes

For workloads needing more than 16,000 IOPS or >1,000 MB/s, you can RAID multiple EBS volumes inside the OS:
- **RAID 0**: stripes data; increases IOPS and throughput, no redundancy.
- **RAID 1**: mirrors; increases durability, no performance boost.

This is advanced but demonstrates the flexibility of block storage.
